CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left-sided lower back pain. History of back surgery in November 2020 for microdiscectomy due to herniated disk that wrapped around spinal thecal sac. Previously experienced severe nerve pain down leg and was on high-dose gabapentin with difficult withdrawal. Currently has pain in left lower back area, generally around where surgery was performed, though location varies day to day. Stretching helps alleviate pain. Pain worsens with bending over and occurs randomly. Patient denies pain down legs. Currently taking ibuprofen 800 mg daily. Has not tried icing. No pain with forward flexion or extension on exam, but reports pain with weightbearing.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Microdiscectomy in November 2020

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen 800 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Flexion: No pain with forward bending
Extension: No pain with backward bending
Weightbearing: Pain present while standing
Palpation: Tenderness on left side around L5; no pain on right side
Motor: Dorsiflexion normal, able to push back against resistance
Range of motion: Normal
Neurologic: No pain down legs

RESULTS
X-ray of spine: No fractures, normal spinal bone, surgical site healed properly

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Muscle pull with spinal misalignment status post microdiscectomy. Plan includes: physical therapy referral to VA physical therapist; discontinue ibuprofen and start meloxicam for pain management; prescribe demerol; referral to pain management for discussion of pain management strategies and consideration of non-narcotic approaches.
